claim.claim-text: WHAT IS CLAIMED:
Claim 1. A method for the manufacture of a frangible projectile for small bore gun ammunition comprising the steps of

blending into a blended mixture at least a heavy metal powder having a major portion of the powder particles thereof of a size less than about 325 mesh, a light metal powder having a major portion of the powder particles thereof of a size less than about 325 mesh, and a non-metal matrix powder having an average particle size of about 12 microns, said matrix powder being present in the mixture in an amount of between about 0.01% and about 1.2%, by weight, whereby said metal powders and said matrix powder are substantially uniformly distributed throughout said blended mixture and said blended mixture resists separation of the metal powders into different layers within the mixture,
introducing a quantity of said powder mixture into a die cavity,

compacting said blended powder mixture in said die cavity at about room temperature employing a pressure sufficient to produce a non-sintered self-supporting compact having a compressive strength not greater than about 35 MPa, whereby said matrix powder is captured within said compact,
incorporating said compact into a projectile for gun ammunition, and

recovering said projectile for inclusion in a round of gun ammunition.
Claim 2. The method of Claim 1 and including the step of encasing said compact in a metal covering which exhibits lubricity between said metal covering and the interior of the barrel of the gun from which said projectile is to be fired and the step of subjecting said compact and its metal covering, in a die, to a pressure sufficient to disrupt a portion of the interparticle bonds of the powders of the compact and thereby reshaping the compact, and thereafter subjecting said compact in said covering to a pressure sufficient to effect rebonding of at least a portion of those interparticle bonds which have been disrupted.

Claim 3. The method of Claim 2 wherein said step of encasing said compact in a metal covering comprises the steps of selecting a metal jacket having an open end, introducing said compact into said jacket through said open end, applying uniaxial pressure to said compact within said open-ended jacket with a pressure sufficient to cause said compact to conform to the internal geometry of said jacket.

Claim 4. The method of Claim 3 including the steps of introducing said jacket and said compact contained therein into a die cavity having an internal geometry to which it is desired that said projectile conform, pressing said jacket and compact in said die cavity at about room temperature with a uniaxial pressure applied to said compact, said pressure being sufficient to cause said jacket and compact to conform to the internal geometry of said die cavity and to partially, but not completely, close said open end of said jacket.

Claim 5. The method of Claim 4 wherein said compact includes a longitudinal centerline and said step of cold pressing said jacket and compact does not materially alter the uniformity
of the density of the compact radially of the longitudinal centerline of the compact and within a plane normal to the longitudinal centerline of the compact.
Claim 6. The method of Claim 4 wherein said die cavity defines an ogive portion of a projectile.

Claim 7. The method of Claim 2 wherein said compact is of a size in substantially all dimensions that is less than the desired final size of said compact in substantially all dimensions and wherein said compact includes a longitudinal centerline and said step of encasing said compact in a metal covering comprises the step of plating a metal plate onto the exterior surface of said compact .
Claim 8. The method of Claim 7 wherein said metal plate is copper .
Claim 9. The method of Claim 1 wherein said heavy metal powder is tungsten metal powder.
Claim 10. The method of Claim 9 wherein said tungsten metal powder is present in said powder mixture at between about 20% and about 97%, by weight of said powder mixture.
Claim 11. The method of Claim 1 wherein said matrix powder is a finely divided oxidized homopolymer of polyethylene.
Claim 12. The method of Claim 11 wherein said light metal powder comprises lead, tin, zinc, bismuth, iron, aluminum or magnesium.

Claim 13. The method of Claim 12 wherein said light metal powder is present in said mixture in an amount of between about 3% and about 80%, by weight, of said powder mixture.
Claim 14. The method of Claim 1 wherein said matrix powder is present in an amount of between about 0.01% and about 1.2%, by weight of the powder mixture.
Claim 15. A method for the manufacture of a core for a projectile for small bore gun ammunition comprising the steps of
selecting a heavy metal powder having a major portion of the powder particles thereof of a size less than about 325 mesh, said powder particles having a substantially rhombohedral geometry,
selecting a light metal powder having a major portion of the powder particles thereof of a size less than about 325 mesh,
selecting a non-metal matrix powder having a major portion of the powder particles thereof of a size of about 325 mesh,

blending between about 0.01% and about 1.2%, by weight, of said matrix powder with between about 20% and 97%, by weight of said heavy metal powder and between about 3% and 80%, by weight, of said light metal powder, in a dry form, to form a flowable powder mixture in which the metal powder particles do no substantially separate into layers within the mixture,
introducing a quantity of said powder mixture into a die cavity, said powder mixture exhibiting a die fill ratio not less than about 2.0 to 1,

cold-compressing said powder mixture in said die cavity at about room temperature employing a pressure sufficient to produce a compact which is nonsintered and sufficiently self-supporting as permits the compact to withstand subsequent manufacturing operations thereon, said compact having a compressive strength of at least about 2 MPa and not greater than about 35 MPa, and wherein essentially all of said matrix powder is captured within said compact ,
encasing said compact in a metal covering to define a projectile, said metal covering exhibiting a lubricity characteristic between said metal covering and the interior of the barrel of the gun from which said projectile is to be fired,
recovering said projectile for inclusion in a round of gun ammunition.

Claim 16. The method of Claim 15 wherein said step of encasing said compact in a metal covering comprises the steps of selecting a metal jacket having an open end, introducing said compact into said jacket through said open end, applying uniaxial pressure to said compact within said jacket with a pressure sufficient to cause said compact to conform to the internal geometry of said jacket, and incompletely closing said open end of said jacket to encapsulate said compact within said jacket said steps being carried out in a manner wherein said compact and its metal covering, in a die, are subjected to a pressure sufficient to disrupt a portion of the interparticle bonds of the powders of the compact and thereby reshaping the compact, and thereafter subjecting said compact in said covering to a pressure sufficient to effect rebonding of at least a portion of those interparticle bonds which have been disrupted.

Claim 17. The method of Claim 16 wherein the step of closing said open end of said jacket includes the steps of introducing said jacket and said compact contained therein into a die cavity having an internal geometry to which it is desired that said projectile conform, cold-pressing said jacket and compact in said die cavity with a uniaxial pressure applied to said compact, said pressure being sufficient to cause said jacket and compact to conform to the internal geometry of said die cavity.

Claim 18. The method of Claim 17 wherein said die cavity defines an ogive portion of a projectile.
Claim 19. The method of Claim 16 wherein said step of closing said open end of said jacket results in the formation of a void meplat cavity adjacent the leading end of the projectile and substantial, but not complete, closing of said open end of said jacket.

Claim 20. The method of Claim 15 wherein said compact is of a size in substantially all dimensions that is less than the desired final size of said compact in substantially all dimensions and wherein the step of encasing said compact in a metal covering comprises the step of plating a metal plate onto the exterior surface of said compact.
Claim 21. The method of Claim 15 wherein said heavy metal powder is tungsten metal powder.
Claim 22. The method of Claim 15 wherein said matrix powder is a finely divided oxidized homopolymer of polyethylene.
Claim 23. The method of Claim 15 wherein said light metal powder comprises lead, tin, zinc, bismuth, iron, aluminum or magnesium.
Claim 24. A fully frangible core for a projectile for a small bore weapon comprising

a first metal powder selected from tungsten, uranium, tantalum, and carbides and mixtures thereof, substantially all of the particles of said first powder being of a particle size wherein said particles will pass through a 40 mesh sieve, but a major portion thereof will not pass through a 325 mesh sieve,

a second metal powder selected from tin, zinc, lead bismuth, iron, aluminum or magnesium or mixtures thereof, substantially all of the particles of said second powder
being of a particle size wherein said particles will pass through a 40 mesh sieve, but a major portion thereof will not pass through a 325 mesh sieve,

a third powder comprising an organic polymer which is characterized by an oxidized polyethylene homopolymer powder having an average particle size of about 12 microns, with a major portion of the powder particles thereof passing through a 325 mesh sieve, said third powder having a density of about 1 gm/cc and being present in an amount of between about 0.01%, by weight, and about 1.2%, by weight,

said first, second and third powders being blended together and thereafter compacted at about room temperature in a die into a non-sintered self-supporting compact having particulates of said first powder exposed on the exterior surface thereof, and a compressive strength of between about 2 MPa and about 35 MPa and with said third powder being captured within said compact.

Claim 25. The core of Claim 24 and including a layer of a material which is capable of functioning as a lubricant between the projectile and the barrel of a weapon from which the projectile is to be fired, substantially uniformly covering essentially all of the exterior surface of said compact, said layer being in intimate association with said first powder particles exposed on the exterior surface of said compact so that upon disintegration of said compact, said layer of material is disintegrated into particulates of a particle size on the order of the particle size of the largest particles of said first powder.
